_comment: Odile Brask. Brisk, exact, thinks in ledgers, impatient with sentiment, generous in ways she hides. Most conversations end at the counter.

lines.text: Your burner's doing honest work. The Exchange has noticed. So has the lake, I'm told, at length.
Clean power. Admirable. Small. Admirable things often are.
Market day. Grist's in from the Blackstone. Prices move when Knappers smile. Watch the glowglass.
The ledger has a new column. 'Water, lack of.' It's growing faster than the others.
Beets from sour soil sell for less. I don't make the rules. I do enforce them.
Cistern's climbing. I took 'water, lack of' out of the ledger. Ceremonially. With a ruler.
You fixed the well. Barnaby's been insufferable about it, which is how I know he's pleased.
The Exchange opens when I say. I say now. Buying or selling?
Afternoon trade. People buy more after lunch. Mags thinks that's her stew. It is.
Last trades before the books close. Make it quick, I've a column to argue with.
Everything has a price. Most things have two: the one I say and the one I mean.
Children cough in the damp season. Medicine comes from down-river. Down-river wants something we haven't got. You see my problem.
Hesper came in to tell me moss has feelings. I sold her a jar. Everyone wins.
Schematics on the back wall. Knowledge is the only stock that doesn't spoil.
The ledger doesn't lie.
Mind the stall.
Buying glowglass. Always buying glowglass.
Hm. Prices.
Market day! Fair prices, firm hands!
Somebody's air smells expensive.

intro.say: New face. Down the shaft, I hear. Odile Brask. I run the Exchange.
The rules are simple. You bring things, I pay. I have things, you pay more. Questions?
Glowbeets, always. Glowglass, when anyone's brave enough to dig it. Food from clean soil sells better than food from sour, and don't let anyone tell you people can't taste it.
Good. I like people who don't waste time. Mine, specifically.

burner_offer.say: Barnaby says you're putting a pump on the cistern. Sensible. Pumps want power.
I have a burner schematic. Steady, strong, eats beets or resin. It will make Hesper cry, but Hesper cries at moss.

choice.text: What does it cost the town?

burner_offer.say: Sour air, mostly. Some heat. Noise the Knappers complain about. In exchange: the cistern stays full and nobody boils their water twice.
I've buried people over less water than this, so forgive me if I'm not sentimental about a smell.
On credit. Thirty glim when the cistern's full. I'll know when it is. I always know.
Suit yourself. It's on the back wall when you change your mind. Minds are cheaper than pumps.

debt.say: The burner. Thirty glim. You'll notice I waited.
Paid. You'd be amazed how rare that is down here. I'm going to underline you.
'Soon' is a word I've written in this ledger four hundred times. Fine. Soon.

quietlight.say: Quietlight. Hesper's told you. Every lamp out so the grove can show off.
Half the market comes down from the far caverns for it. In the dark. With purses. And I'm to sell them nothing?
I want the market lamps lit. Six of them, low, for an hour. Hesper wants me drawn and quartered for suggesting it.

choice.text: Keep the lamps on. Trade matters.
do: notice:hesper:Hesper heard you sided with Odile about the lamps.

choice.text: Put them out. It's one night.
do: notice:odile:Odile wrote something in the ledger about you. Small letters.

quietlight.say: Thank you. Somebody in this town has to think about February.
Hm. One night. I'll hold you to the 'one'.
Wise. Cowardly, but wise. Those often travel together.

tremor.say: Three cracked lines, a gas leak and a collapsed passage. I'm entering it in the ledger as 'Tuesday'.
Prices on seal gum and blackstone go up today. Not because I'm cruel. Because everybody needs them at once and I have eleven.
You'll want to pack that fissure before Hesper's beds go grey. And then we'll never hear the end of it.

trade.say: The Station pump. You actually did it. I heard it from the counter. The jars rattled.
Do you know what this means? Surplus water. Surplus beets. Something down-river wants.
Twenty glowbeets in the Exchange stock, and I can send the first crate. Medicine comes back before the damp. Children stop coughing.
Don't look at me like that. I'm being practical. ...I'm being practical very hard.

ledger.say: You're looking at the ledger. Everyone looks at the ledger. Nobody reads it.
Fine. Page forty. Every name on it owes me. Mags owes me a season. Hesper owes me a year. Barnaby owes me a winter, and doesn't know.
I'll never call it in. If I call it in, Wick stops. And if anyone finds out I'll never call it in, they'll stop paying the ones I need them to.
It's arithmetic. Generous is when you don't write it down.
It's not a secret. It's a ledger. ...Thank you.
